data.long_meaning: The name Octavio is derived from the Latin word ‘octavus’, which means ‘eighth’. It was commonly used as a personal name during the Roman Republic and Empire due to its association with the number eight, which was considered a symbol of good fortune and prosperity. The name Octavio carries the meaning “Eighth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Octavio usually hope their child will grow to embody eighth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.long_meaning: Οκτάβιο είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό Octavius, που σημαίνει ο όγδοος. Στη Βίβλο, ο αριθμός οκτώ συμβολίζει τη νέα αρχή και την πληρότητα. Το όνομα Οκτάβιο συνδέεται με την παράδοση των οκταβικών αριθμών και τη σημασία τους στην ιστορία της Εκκλησίας.

data.cultural_impact: The name Octavio has ties to ancient Roman history and culture. It was a popular name among the Roman nobility due to its association with the number Eight, a symbol of good fortune and power. Additionally, Octavian (Octavius in Latin) is the name of the first Roman emperor, Augustus Caesar, who took power after the civil wars following Julius Caesar's assassination.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the number eight symbolizes new beginnings and resurrection. This significance can be traced back to the Old Testament where there were eight individuals saved in the Ark of Noah during the great flood, representing a new beginning. Also, Jesus rose from the dead on the third day but was fully resurrected on the eighth day. Thus, the name Octavio can be seen as a reminder of the power of new beginnings and resurrection in the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Octavio, meaning 'eighth' in Latin, symbolizes the idea of new beginnings and the cycle of life. In Christianity, it represents the eighth day, the day of rebirth, and the belief that every day brings the potential for renewal and growth.

historical_references.reference: Octavian (63 BC - 14 AD) was a Roman general and statesman who rose to power after the assassination of Julius Caesar. He took the name Augustus in 27 BC and founded the Roman Empire.
historical_references.context: Octavian was a key figure in the power struggle following Caesar's assassination. He allied with Mark Antony and Marcus Lepidus to form the Second Triumvirate. After defeating Sextus Pompey in the Third Civil War, Octavian became the sole ruler of the Roman Republic, and later assumed the title Augustus and established the Roman Empire.

historical_references.reference: Octavianus (died 117 AD) was a Roman senator and consul who lived during the Roman Empire. He was a patron of the arts and built several important structures in Rome.
historical_references.context: Octavianus was a wealthy and influential figure in Roman society during the reign of Trajan. He was a patron of the arts and helped fund the construction of several important structures in Rome, including the Basilica Ulpia and the Baths of Trajan.
